messages:
anya: thinking out loud — what if we add a short-lived per-tenant micro-lane that buffers arrivals for up to 8–15ms (or until a small local batch forms) before injecting into the global coalescer? idea is to sandbox noisy tiny tenants so they don't smash the global KV cache / coalesce shape

sahil: curious — sandboxing sounds good for jitter isolation but wont that reduce global packing and hurt throughput for steady tenants?

kevin: we ran something like this last year (soft-lanes prototype). tradeoff: p99 tail improved for small-tenants, overall token throughput dropped ~10-12% under high cardinality. memory usage went up because of queued payloads.

infra-bot: perf-run: sandbox-lanes-v3 — p50 32ms -> 30ms, p95 96ms -> 88ms, p99 142ms -> 129ms, throughput -11.4%, peak mem +21%

zara: another problem: KV-cache affinity. if micro-lanes hold requests, KV handles might be retained longer and block eviction signals. we need a lease/ownership tag so cache eviction can treat those handles as low-priority.

anya: exactly — thought of two mitigations: (1) strengthen headroom accounting per-lane (mem + kv handles) with a soft cap, (2) fast-path fallback: if global headroom low, drain lane immediately into global coalescer (no holding).

kevin: +1 for fallback. also need fairness credits so a tenant doesnt repeatedly land in sandbox and starve themselves. i.e. adaptive time cap based on recent bypasses.

sahil: sketch of adaptive cap: 
```
cap = base_ms * (1 + min( max_small_tenant_score, 3 ))
if mem_usage_fraction > 0.8: cap = 0  // bypass sandbox
```
where small_tenant_score = recent QPS variance / mean.

tomas: ops note — when we tried a variant, GPUs showed ~18% higher host memory pressure because request objects queued on CPU. need guardrails: per-host lane budget + eviction watermark so OS oom isn't near.

zara: we also need an explicit KV lease TTL on micro-lane handles. something like 50ms TTL then either renew (if lane still buffering) or release. also tag telemetry: `kv_handle_held_ms` and `lane_bypass_reason`

anya: for rollout plan: feature-flagged canary on 10% hosts, measure p99 latency for small tenants, overall throughput, peak mem, kv_evict_rate. fallback rule: if peak_mem delta > 12% OR throughput drop > 8% -> auto-disable.

kevin: metrics to add: `scheduler.sandboxed_requests`, `scheduler.lane_hold_time_ms`, `scheduler.bypasses_per_tenant`, and `scheduler.sandbox_hit_ratio` — plus KPI for KV eviction stalls.

zara: i'll prepare a canary job. flag name: `runtime.sched.sandbox_microlane.v1` — will gate on `enable && host_budget_ok`

sahil: i'll draft the runtime change (admission + lane bookkeeping + telemetry). assigning to `runtime-scheduler` team for RFC -> PR. gonna outline API: 
```
struct MicroLaneConfig {
  max_hold_ms: int;
  max_bytes: int;
  kv_lease_ttl_ms: int;
  bypass_if_mem_frac: float;
}
```

anya: one more UX/observability thought — tag traces: `lane=microlane` and `lane=global` so we can correlate per-tenant quality. also add a slow-path reason code in responses when bypassed.

kevin: SG. let's avoid naming collisions with other lane features. also add an experiment id header so we can A/B.

zara: i'll open the canary job + feature flag and post link here when ready :eyes:

anya: great — thanks. next steps: sahil to write RFC + perf harness plan, zara to own canary, kevin to add requested metrics in statsd proto. i can coordinate rollout criteria. :+1:

sahil: will do. ping me if you want to pair on the eviction TTL bits.

zara: linking the perf job when created — will annotate with test parameters and host mem limits.

anya: ok closing thread for now, moving details to the rfc doc (rfc/runtime/0000-microlane-sandbox.md) and the PR tracker.
